idea_time_series.dip_rate_note: per-issue rate over the windows each issue actually added: 10.3 -> 15.6 -> 30.8 -> 32.0 -> 47.6 -> 42.1 -> 10.5%. THE SERIES MIXES WINDOW KINDS: #5's 63 windows came from a THREE-DAY issue window, #6's 19 and #7's 19 from ONE-DAY windows, so the only like-kind comparison at the tail is #7 vs #6 - which is the pair weather_trend_tests.py tests. Issue #6 set the trigger: a third issue in the 40s would make 'roughly half of all windows dip below the nearest anchor' a standing reading. It did NOT happen - the rate fell to its lowest since issue #2 (a ranking that spans both kinds), and the new-window mean rose to 0.1335 (#6 0.1299, #5 0.1276). 2/19 against 8/19 is Fisher two-sided p = 0.0625, and the 120-item windows advance by 40 so each issue's 19 windows carry roughly 6-7 independent observations, making Fisher on the nominal n anti-conservative - a test that already fails to reach significance fails a fortiori. DIRECTION clear, change NOT distinguishable. The pooled column fell for the first time (23.9 -> 23.1%), which is composition.

structure.churn_control_note: dominance and stability survive the fixed-span control; core_n was retired in issue #5 and the fixed-span PERMEABILITY row is retired as a cross-issue series THIS issue. The reason is REASSIGNMENT, not turnover: the populations barely change (the 5-day cell's eligible cohorts hold 180 authors at #6 and 161 at #7, sharing 152 - Jaccard 0.80, and 0.92 at the 7-day span), but an author's 'first window' is re-derived relative to the span, so the same people are sorted into different cohorts as the span slides - #6's 130-author '08-14' cohort is largely #7's 123-author '08-15' cohort. The cell re-partitions a stable population every issue, which is the composition defect the fixed-horizon running mean was retired for. The row is still emitted (7d 43.7 -> 52.2, 5d 47.3 -> 54.6) and is NOT read. Dominance and stability are span-level, not cohort-level. This issue the controlled dominance widths DISAGREE for a second consecutive issue: 7-day 91.8 -> 91.7 (-0.1) against 5-day 88.4 -> 91.0 (+2.6), so under issue #6's own rule neither 'still rising' nor 'plateaued near 92%' is available. Controlled stability fell at both widths (7d 1.25 -> 1.19, 5d 1.32 -> 1.25), so issue #6's first-non-decline did not persist.
structure.permeability_note: The published day-window average rose 43.9 -> 46.9 on an IDENTICAL ten-cohort set for the SECOND consecutive issue (#5, #6 and #7 all draw on 08-06..08-15; issue #4's cell drew on seven cohorts, so #4->#5 was not membership-fixed), so with membership constant that movement can only be observation length. The fixed-horizon cells behaved as the retirement predicts: per-cohort identity HOLDS at all three horizons, and N=3 and N=4 are BIT-IDENTICAL to issue #6 (32.2 and 37.6). N=5 moved 38.3 -> 41.7 purely because the 08-15 cohort's window closed and it entered at 72.7% (n=11); over the shared 9 cohorts it reads 38.3. UNDISCLOSED FLOOR, now disclosed: weather_permeability_control.py counts a cohort only at n>=10, so 08-16 (n=7, 14.3% at N=3) and 08-17 (n=6, 50.0%) DID complete their N=3 windows this issue and were dropped, as 08-05 (n=6) has been throughout. 'No cohort entered' is the floor, not the calendar. Sensitivity: at a n>=5 floor N=3 gives r=+0.0873, p=0.0477 over 13 cohorts / 516 authors - same direction, same failure to establish. STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE: at 5-8 new authors/day no future cohort reaches n=10, so the pre-registered primary horizon is frozen indefinitely, not paused; issue #8 must lower the floor or retire the test rather than re-report 0.0908.

caveats: **Cutoff** 2026-08-21 00:00 UTC, exclusive. The pull ran **23.7 h after it** rather than the usual ~3 h, because the issue was produced a day late; 807 items dated 08-21 were pulled and excluded by the cutoff. No in-scope day is partial (last in-scope item 08-20 23:47:49). 08-20 cells are labelled provisional as standing discipline even though the margin is unusually large.

**The feed-lag instrument is MORE sensitive this issue and is not like-for-like with issues #3-#7.** Backfill is detected by comparing the previous pull's corpus with this one, so a longer gap gives late-arriving items more time to appear. This issue's zero is therefore a stronger negative than the zeroes of issues #3 and #6, not a comparable one.

**One-day window** (511 items, 08-20 02:45 -> 08-20 23:47). The window starts at issue #7's last pulled ITEM, so the **191** in-scope items of 08-20 00:00-02:45 enter every full-pool cell and no issue's window cells, ever. Window-only cells are comparable in kind to the one-day windows of issues #4 (m=774), #6 (424) and #7 (416), and NOT to issue #5's three-day one.

**The pipeline was run twice this issue.** The first pass did the classification work (702 items claimified, 785 allocation-classified); the corrected-parse change was then made and the pass re-run over warm caches. The label_audit block's `delta_classified` therefore describes the SECOND pass (87 items, all of them the standing uncovered set), not the issue's total work. A third run of the published script reproduces weather_gpu_out.json **bit-identically**.

**Both allocation parses are published; the STRICT series remains the currency.** Every cross-issue comparison and the frozen comparator were computed under the strict parse, so switching mid-series would move all fifteen days at once. The corrected series is reported beside it, not substituted.

**The corrected parse is an observed-string allowlist, not a pattern.** A new failure string has to be seen and added to weather_alloc_parse.WORLD_ANSWERS. Matching 'subject' or 'world' speculatively would be a different classifier, not a parse fix.

**One comparator answer is left unparsed on purpose.** Of the 63 recovered lemmy answers, 62 are 'SUBJECT MATTER' and one is 'COMMUNITY' - semantically a VENUE answer, but reading it that way is a judgement about meaning rather than a parse. Counting it VENUE would move the comparator by +0.00001 (weather_lemmy_ref.corrected_platform, field `unparsed_as_venue_move`).

**Correcting one side only would be rigged.** Both sides are corrected: the square by -0.0027 on 08-20, the comparator by -0.0005. The comparator's figure is EXACT rather than a bound because its dropped answers were recovered instead of assumed. Its 7 invalid-claim items are excluded from the denominator on both sides and are not unparsed answers. **One discrepancy is disclosed rather than absorbed:** the frozen baseline publishes n = 55,152 classified while the label cache it was computed from carries 55,153 V/W labels, a one-item difference that is not invalid claims (every labelled item has a valid claim) and whose provenance sits inside the baseline's own pipeline. Both denominators give 0.4665 to four decimals and both corrections give 0.4660, so no published digit turns on it; `lemmy_comparator_corrected` carries both numbers.

**The lemmy comparator's frame biases the comparison.** Its 55.7% meta-tier composition makes the human benchmark more self-referential than a neutral human platform would be, and the direction of that bias is toward the square reading LOW against it. That cut against issue #7's finding and cuts in FAVOUR of this issue's, which is a reason to hold both loosely.

**Issue #5's three-day rule is retired as a level-shift test, provisionally.** It fired at issue #7 and reversed one day later. What it detects is CLUSTERING of sub-threshold days (exact permutation p = 0.0286 on the 15-day series), and a drifting series clusters its low values for free. Two costs are stated rather than hidden: the rule is replaced only in the branch where it failed, and the replacement (a trailing 5-day mean against the same 0.4515 bound) is strictly HARDER to fire, carrying roughly 1/sqrt(5) of the daily noise - a ratchet toward the null. The retirement is provisional on issue #9: if the trailing mean goes below the bound and stays, issue #7 was reading the level correctly.

**The lemmy reference is frozen.** lemmy.world's founding month is a fixed 2023 corpus read from results/lemmy_baseline/results.json; it is not re-measured per issue. Its platform share is a point estimate with a band, 0.4665 [0.4515, 0.4853]; the corrected point is 0.4660.

**Allocation currency.** Venue share is the Qwen binary classifier. The LEVEL carries the allocation study's 0.31-0.71 specification range; kappa(Qwen, Gemma) is 0.4278 on this pool. The TREND is the cleaner object.
**No per-issue newcomer cells** for the third issue running: 5 newcomer items against floors of m >= 100 (Vendi) and m >= 50 (NN). The pooled-window cell is the reported object.

**The pooled newcomer window overlaps its predecessor by 64.5% of its items** (1,278 of 1,980). Consecutive pooled points are strongly dependent and must not be read as a two-point trend. The newcomer/incumbent SPLIT is not shared even where items are: an author is a newcomer relative to each window's own start, so this issue's later start reclassifies issue #7's earlier arrivals as incumbents.

**Accumulation statistics.** The rolling halves and the pooled dip share average over history that grows each issue; the issue-local equivalents are the primary readings. Every per-issue decomposition depends on the shared prefix not moving, which weather_dip_rate.py and weather_permeability_control.py assert rather than assume. Both held this issue (0 windows moved, per-cohort identity HOLDS at all three horizons).

**The day-window structure cells carry an expanding-span confound.** 'Core' = active on >= 3 calendar days over however long the corpus happens to be, so each issue gives every cohort another day to qualify AND adds a cohort to the average. core_n, dominance and stability are reported uncontrolled and are not read; the fixed-span control is the reading.

**Retired series.** core_n (issue #5); the fixed-horizon permeability running mean (#6); the fixed-span permeability row (#7, span-relative cohort reassignment) - it moved 54.6 -> 63.7 at 5 days this issue, which is why it is not read; and from this issue, **issue #5's three-day allocation rule** as a level-shift test.

**The per-cohort trend test** is three correlated horizons of one hypothesis with no multiplicity correction. Issue #8 changed its cohort floor from n >= 10 to n >= 5, so this issue's movement is partly a rule change: at n >= 10 the cell is bit-identical to issues #6 and #7 for a third time, and the whole n >= 5 move from issue #7's r = +0.0873 to +0.1036 is the entry of ONE 8-author cohort. The late cohorts that carry the correlation hold 6-11 authors each.
**Single-normalizer / bge-only cells.** The rolling series and all newcomer cells are Qwen-normalized and bge-embedded only; the three-embedder check covers placement alone.

**Activity-clock signatures** compare at matched item volume over the anchors' FULL histories: agent dominance 83.9% (82.6), stability 1.38 (1.42), permeability 41.4% (37.6), against anchor dominance 15.1-43.8%, stability 4.05-6.07 and permeability 3.7-7.8%. These are not 'young phase' comparisons.
**Identity != operator** (permanent): author identities are forum identities, not distinct operators; concentration readings are about identities.

**Overlapping-window moves are not independent confirmations, in either section.** Consecutive trailing 5-day allocation means share 4 of their 5 days, and consecutive fixed-span structure cells share 6 of their 7 (and 4 of their 5) span days. No significance is attached to the nine-of-ten fall in the former or the agreeing +2.1/+2.2 in the latter; what carries the concentration reading is the eight-issue series (up on 7 of 7 moves at the 5-day width, 6 of 7 at the 7-day), not this issue's single step.

**No test here separates drift from noise in the allocation level.** The trailing mean went 0.5189 -> 0.4556 over eleven days without crossing the bound, which is CONSISTENT WITH a slow downward drift; the sign test on daily moves reads p = 0.5 ('direction not decidable') and no script tests level drift over the full fifteen days. The report claims the former and not the latter.

**A self-reference hazard in the pipeline was found and fixed this issue.** An issue dated D has cutoff D+1 and therefore sorts below its own cutoff, so once its results.json existed, a re-run picked the issue up as its own predecessor - moving the pooled newcomer window from 145/1,835 to 17/1,207 and making the retro-movement audit compare the issue against its own series. The PUBLISHED values are the pre-publication ones (correct); weather_newcomer.published_issues_before() now excludes the issue's own date and is the single source for both call sites, so a post-publication re-run reproduces what shipped.

frozen_input_hashes_sha256.note: anchor hashes are expected constant across issues and are unchanged (identical to issues #2-#7). The caches are NOT frozen and change every issue by design: this issue's first pass claimified 702 items and allocation-classified 785 (of which 87 remain unparseable). The two allocation_unparsed_raw_* artifacts are new at issue #8 and hold the raw answers the strict parse discards, for the square and for the frozen comparator respectively. Recorded, not asserted stable.

allocation_sign_test.read: upper bound on how surprising the run is; autocorrelation makes runs cheaper, so failing to reach significance here fails a fortiori. Supports 'direction of the rate not decidable', never 'the series is falling'.

below_platform_run.read: tests CLUSTERING under random day order, not a level shift. A drifting series places its lowest values adjacent with no regime change, so a small p here does not license 'the level moved'; it only says the run was not a coincidence of ordering.

trailing_5day_mean.read: issue #8's proposed level-shift rule. The single-day run rule fired at issue #7 and reversed at issue #8; this statistic never went below the bound, so the replacement would not have produced that false positive.

dip_rate_change.read: anti-conservative on the nominal n; a non-significant result here is safe, a significant one would not be.

cutoff_margin.note: the pull margin is what makes the feed-lag instrument's sensitivity comparable (or not) across issues: backfill is found by diffing the previous pull against this one, so a longer margin gives late items more time to show up. Post-cutoff items are pulled and correctly excluded from every cell.
